systemz = read.csv(text = '

## Overview

This report presents a rooftop solar potential assessment for the **Bunbury** site
(53.114°N, −2.646°E), covering the period `r date_start` to `r date_end`. Seven
distinct roof surfaces have been identified and characterised.

Solar irradiance estimates are derived from pre-processed ECMWF ERA5 reanalysis data, with shading
calculated from Environment Agency LiDAR digital surface models. Where structures
such as outbuildings or sheds sit above ground level, the DSM is adjusted upward to
reflect their true rooftop height before shading is computed.

## Site and system parameters

The table below summarises the seven roof surfaces included in the analysis. Surfaces
without a recorded aspect and slope have these values extracted directly from the
LiDAR-derived terrain model at the centroid location. Panel counts reflect the
estimated maximum capacity of each surface.

```{r, error=FALSE,echo=FALSE,warning=FALSE}
systemz |>
  select(
    `Surface` = name,
    `Latitude` = lat,
    `Longitude` = lon,
    `Length max (m)` = length_max,
    `Width max (m)` = width_max,
    `Panels` = n_panels,
    `Height above ground (m)` = height,
    `Aspect (°)` = aspect,
    `Slope (°)` = slope
  ) |>
  kable(digits = 4, align = "c") |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                full_width = FALSE) |>
  footnote(general = "Aspect: degrees clockwise from north. NA = derived from LiDAR aspect raster.")
```

## Method

### Meteorological data

Hourly surface solar irradiance (global horizontal, direct normal, and diffuse
horizontal components) is sourced from the **ECMWF ERA5** reanalysis archive via the
`ecmwfr` package. Data are downloaded for a 40 m buffer domain around the site
centroid and aggregated to daily totals. ERA5 has a native spatial resolution of
~31 km; point-level estimates are extracted by bilinear interpolation to the site
coordinates.

Plane-of-array irradiance for each surface is computed from the horizontal components
using the surface tilt and azimuth, accounting for direct beam projection, isotropic
diffuse sky, and ground-reflected components. Where aspect and slope are not
recorded in the system parameters, values are taken from the LiDAR-derived rasters
described below.

### LiDAR digital surface model and shading

A 1 m resolution Digital Surface Model (DSM) is retrieved from the **Environment
Agency National LiDAR Programme** (via `nexurbr::get_gb_lidar()`), covering the
local domain. The DSM represents the top surface of all features — buildings,
vegetation, and ground — in metres above Ordnance Datum (OSGB36/EPSG:27700).

Slope and aspect rasters are derived from the DSM using an 8-neighbour algorithm
(`terra::terrain()`). Monthly shading fractions are then calculated using
`nexurbr::calc_shade()`, which casts solar position vectors (sun azimuth and
elevation at sub-hourly resolution) across the DSM to identify shadowed cells for
each timestep.

### DSM adjustment for above-ground structures

Two roof surfaces (6 and 7) are located on structures with a recorded height above
the surrounding ground plane (3 m). Where height values are provided in the system
parameters, the DSM cell values at those locations are raised by the stated height
before shading is computed. This ensures that the shading model correctly represents
the elevated surface and that neighbouring obstructions are assessed relative to the
true panel position rather than the ground.

The adjustment is applied to a 1 m buffer polygon around the centroid of each
elevated surface, rasterised to the DSM grid.

### Yield calculation

Panel-level yield (kWh/panel/day) is computed using `nexurbr::calc_solar_potential_point()`,
combining plane-of-array irradiance with a standard system efficiency assumption.
Bank-level yield is the product of per-panel yield and panel count. Results are
aggregated to monthly and annual totals for reporting.

## Data preparation

```{r, error=FALSE,echo=FALSE,warning=FALSE}
local_domain = nexurbr::create_domain_polygon(
  latitude  = lat,
  longitude = lon,
  buffer_dist = 40
) |> st_as_sf()
```

```{r, error=FALSE,echo=FALSE,warning=FALSE}
date_df = create_dates_df(
  start_date = date_start,
  end_date   = date_end,
  time_zone  = "UTC",
  timestep   = "day"
)
```

```{r, error=FALSE,echo=FALSE,warning=FALSE}
dsm = get_gb_lidar(domain = local_domain, product = "dsm", product_type = "elevation")

slope_r  = terra::terrain(dsm, v = "slope",  unit = "degrees", neighbors = 8)
aspect_r = terra::terrain(dsm, v = "aspect", unit = "degrees", neighbors = 8)
```

```{r, error=FALSE,echo=FALSE,warning=FALSE}
# Raise DSM at elevated structure locations (surfaces with recorded height)
if (any(!is.na(systemz$height))) {
  s_df = systemz[!is.na(systemz$height), ]
  pts  = st_as_sf(s_df, coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326)

  panel_loc = pts |>
    sf::st_transform(terra::crs(dsm)) |>
    sf::st_buffer(1)

  panel_cells  = terra::rasterize(terra::vect(panel_loc), dsm)
  panel_height = s_df$height
  dsm[!is.na(panel_cells)] = dsm[!is.na(panel_cells)] + panel_height
}
```

```{r, error=FALSE,echo=FALSE,warning=FALSE}
shade = calc_shade(
  start_date  = date_start,
  end_date    = date_end,
  dsm,
  detail      = "monthly",
  omit_nights = TRUE,
  can_grnd    = "canopy"
)
```

```{r, error=FALSE,echo=FALSE,warning=FALSE}
site_meteo = create_meteo_df(
  latitude   = lat,
  longitude  = lon,
  site_name  = site,
  start_date = date_start,
  end_date   = date_end
)
```

## Yield calculation

```{r, error=FALSE,echo=FALSE,warning=FALSE}
yield_list = list()
for (s in systemz$name){
  
  sys_df = filter(systemz, name == s)
  
  aspect_raster = is.na(sys_df$aspect)
  slope_raster = is.na(sys_df$slope)
  
  if(aspect_raster){
    aspect_in = aspect_r
  } else {
    aspect_in = sys_df$aspect
  }
  
  if(slope_raster){
    slope_in = slope_r
  } else {
    slope_in = sys_df$slope
  }

  
tot_solar = calc_solar_potential_point(meteo_dat = site_meteo,
                                       latitude = sys_df$lat,
                                       longitude = sys_df$lon,
                                       aspect = aspect_in,
                                       slope = slope_in,
                                       use_shading = TRUE,
                                       shade_rast = shade
                                       )

tot_solar$kwh_bank = tot_solar$yield_kwh_panel*sys_df$n_panels
tot_solar$bank = sprintf("%02d", sys_df$name)

yield_list[[s]] = tot_solar

}

all_banks = do.call(rbind,yield_list)

all_b_yr = all_banks |>
  mutate(year = lubridate::year(date)) |>
  group_by(bank, year) |>
  summarise(
    kwh_bank = sum(kwh_bank, na.rm = TRUE),
    aspect   = mean(aspect_value),
    slope    = mean(slope_value),
    .groups  = "drop"
  )

all_b_mnth = all_banks |>
  mutate(month = lubridate::month(date)) |>
  group_by(month) |>
  summarise(
    kwh_bank = sum(kwh_bank, na.rm = TRUE),
    aspect   = mean(aspect_value),
    slope    = mean(slope_value),
    .groups  = "drop"
  )

b_summed = all_banks |>
  mutate(year = lubridate::year(date)) |>
  group_by(year) |>
  summarise(kwh_bank = sum(kwh_bank, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

all_b_plot = all_banks |>
  group_by(date) |>
  summarise(kwh_total = sum(kwh_bank), .groups = "drop")
```

## Results

### Annual yield by roof surface

The chart below shows estimated annual kWh yield per roof surface (bank) for each
year in the study period. Surfaces 1 (main roof, 33 panels) and 6 (south-facing
shed roof, 12 panels) are expected to dominate total generation.

```{r, error=FALSE,echo=FALSE,warning=FALSE, fig.cap="Annual yield (kWh) by roof surface and year"}
library(ggplot2)
library(lubridate)
library(dplyr)
library(patchwork)

theme_solar = function() {
  theme_minimal(base_family = "IBM Plex Sans") +
    theme(
      plot.background    = element_rect(fill = "#0f1117", colour = NA),
      panel.background   = element_rect(fill = "#0f1117", colour = NA),
      panel.grid.major   = element_line(colour = "#1e2130"),
      panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
      text               = element_text(colour = "#c9d1d9"),
      axis.text          = element_text(colour = "#8b949e"),
      axis.title         = element_text(colour = "#c9d1d9", size = 9),
      strip.text         = element_text(colour = "#c9d1d9", face = "bold"),
      legend.background  = element_rect(fill = "#0f1117", colour = NA),
      legend.key         = element_rect(fill = "#0f1117", colour = NA),
      plot.title         = element_text(colour = "#e6edf3", face = "bold", size = 12),
      plot.subtitle      = element_text(colour = "#8b949e", size = 9),
      plot.margin        = margin(12, 12, 12, 12)
    )
}

pal = c("#f97316","#3b82f6","#10b981","#a855f7","#ec4899","#eab308","#06b6d4")

# 1. Mean diurnal profile (averaging IS correct here — shape of the day)
p_hour = all_banks |>
  mutate(hour = hour(date)) |>
  group_by(hour, bank) |>
  summarise(kwh = mean(kwh_bank), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(hour, kwh, colour = bank)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 1.2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = pal) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 23, 3)) +
  labs(title = "Mean diurnal profile", x = "Hour of day", y = "kWh", colour = "Surface") +
  theme_solar()

# 2. Monthly totals (sum is correct)
p_month = all_banks |>
  mutate(month = floor_date(date, "month")) |>
  group_by(month, bank) |>
  summarise(kwh = sum(kwh_bank), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(month, kwh, fill = bank)) +
  geom_col(width = 25 * 24 * 3600) +  # 25 days in seconds
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal) +
  labs(title = "Monthly yield by surface", x = NULL, y = "kWh", fill = "Surface") +
  theme_solar() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))

# 3. Annual totals (sum)
p_annual = all_banks |>
  mutate(year = year(date)) |>
  group_by(year, bank) |>
  summarise(kwh = sum(kwh_bank), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(factor(year), kwh, fill = bank)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal) +
  labs(title = "Annual yield by surface", x = NULL, y = "kWh", fill = "Surface") +
  theme_solar()

# Combine
p_hour / p_month / p_annual +
  plot_annotation(
    title    = "Solar yield — Bunbury",
    subtitle = "ERA5 irradiance · LiDAR shading · 2020–2025",
    theme    = theme(
      plot.background = element_rect(fill = "#0f1117", colour = NA),
      plot.title      = element_text(colour = "#e6edf3", face = "bold",
                                     size = 14, family = "IBM Plex Sans"),
      plot.subtitle   = element_text(colour = "#8b949e", size = 9,
                                     family = "IBM Plex Sans")
    )
  )


```

```{r, error=FALSE,echo=FALSE,warning=FALSE}
b_summed |>
  rename(Year = year, `Total yield (kWh)` = kwh_bank) |>

```

## Discussion

The analysis draws on six years of ERA5 meteorological data (2020–2025), providing
a representative picture of inter-annual variability driven by cloud cover and
solar geometry at this latitude (~53°N). Yield estimates are sensitive to assumed
panel efficiency and inverter losses, which use standard defaults in this version
of the model; site-specific values can be substituted as they become available.

Shading from neighbouring vegetation and structures is captured in the LiDAR DSM
but is subject to the resolution of the 1 m dataset and the date of the survey
flight. Seasonal variation in deciduous canopy is not accounted for, which may
lead to a modest underestimate of summer yield for surfaces adjacent to trees.

The DSM elevation adjustment for surfaces 6 and 7 (shed roof, +3 m) has a material
effect on shading calculations for those surfaces; without it, the model would
underestimate exposure by treating panels as if at ground level.
```
